Subject: Azura Labs — request for one-off evaluation uplift and term flexibility

Team,

Quick escalation: Azura Labs (Anna Park) is midway through a technically complex evaluation. They hit a blocker that requires us to spin a dedicated VPC preview and run longer multi-model experiments. Their procurement timeline is slow (security/compliance review still open) and they're asking for a small, one-off allowance so engineering can complete feature validation before their budget sign-off.

Ask: approval for a temporary evaluation uplift (complimentary compute credit) and a 30-day extension beyond our standard 14-day PLG trial. This is not a blanket concession — one-off for AZR-142, contingent on procurement timeline milestones.

Why this matters:
- This is a strategic target (healthcare analytics) with clear HIPAA surface. If the evaluation validates, they plan a mid-market committed deployment and a Dedicated capacity conversation.
- They’ve already run a short proof and provided logs; the ask is narrowly scoped to remove false negatives caused by their compliance setup window.

Proposed concession (internal recommendation): 60k token-equivalent credit + 30-day trial extension + prioritized onboarding runbook. No change to list pricing or SLAs. We can require a short mutual action plan (shared milestones) and a procurement PO by end of July.

I’ve attached a one-page tech summary and procurement timeline from Azura. Hoping to accelerate — please advise next steps and whether this needs CRO/CFO sign-off.

Thanks,
Sooj

Thanks Marissa — answers below and I’ve pasted the customer's note at the bottom for traceability.

1) Usage estimate (30-day window):
- Low: 20k token-equiv (light integration tests + a few embeddings jobs)
- Expected: 60k token-equiv (full multi-model experiments, KV cache warmup)
- High: 120k token-equiv (extended stress runs + dataset ingestion)

2) Procurement: they plan to submit a PO that covers the POC month once security signs off. No special invoicing cadence requested — standard net30 is fine. They did ask for a short-term billing hold until the PO is processed; we're not obligated.

3) Security/compliance: they need Private preview (VPC) to connect to internal datasets and HSM-backed KMS for a small subset. They will not move production data — only deidentified test exports.

Customer note (Anna Park, Azura): "We hit a certificate rotation issue in our staging VPC that prevents consistent model access; we need the extra runway to complete the rotation and run full validation. If Redwood can provide a short-term uplift and VPC preview, we can commit to the PO by 7/28."

Suggested guardrails: mutual action plan (milestone-based), limited to AZR-142, require PO submission by 2028-07-28 or credits will be revoked; no SLA changes; no ongoing discount to list rates beyond an introductory committed month.

I uploaded the timeline to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/azura-labs/record-142

Sooj

- One-off complimentary credit: up to 60k token-equivalent (with metrics-based cap and kill-switch)
- Trial extension: +30 days beyond standard PLG period
- Additional: prioritized VPC preview provisioning (internal resource allocation)

Conditions:
- Deal Desk to draft a short concession memo highlighting risk, ROI, and exact kill-switch metrics (e.g., absolute token cap, time window).
